description: Split a string by delimiter into a table of substrings
best_practice_code:
function split(s, delimiter)
    local result = {}
    if s == nil or s == "" then return result end
    if delimiter == nil or delimiter == "" then
        table.insert(result, s)
        return result
    end
    local pattern = "([^" .. delimiter .. "]+)"
    for match in s:gmatch(pattern) do
        table.insert(result, match)
    end
    return result
end

test_assert_eq(#split('', ','), 0, 'split: empty string')
test_assert_eq(#split('hello', ','), 1, 'split: no delimiter')
test_assert_eq(split('hello', ',')[1], 'hello', 'split: no delimiter value')

description: String interpolation and formatting with variables
best_practice_code:
function interpolate(template, vars)
    return template:gsub('{(%w+)}', function(key)
        return tostring(vars[key] or '{' .. key .. '}')
    end)
end

function pad_left(s, length, char)
    char = char or ' '
    s = tostring(s)
    while #s < length do
        s = char .. s
    end
    return s
end

function pad_right(s, length, char)
    char = char or ' '
    s = tostring(s)
    while #s < length do
        s = s .. char
    end
    return s
end
prewritten_tests:

test_assert_eq(interpolate('{missing}', {}), '{missing}', 'interpolate: missing key')
test_assert_eq(pad_left('42', 5, '0'), '00042', 'pad_left')
test_assert_eq(pad_right('hi', 5, '.'), 'hi...', 'pad_right')

description: Map, filter, reduce operations on Lua tables
best_practice_code:
function map(t, fn)
    local result = {}
    for i, v in ipairs(t) do
        result[i] = fn(v, i)
    end
    return result
end

function filter(t, fn)
    local result = {}
    for i, v in ipairs(t) do
        if fn(v, i) then
            table.insert(result, v)
        end
    end
    return result
end

function reduce(t, fn, init)
    local acc = init
    for i, v in ipairs(t) do
        acc = fn(acc, v, i)
    end
    return acc
end

description: Deep copy a Lua table including nested tables
best_practice_code:
function deep_copy(orig)
    if type(orig) ~= 'table' then return orig end
    local copy = {}
    for k, v in pairs(orig) do
        copy[deep_copy(k)] = deep_copy(v)
    end
    return setmetatable(copy, getmetatable(orig))
end

function shallow_copy(orig)
    if type(orig) ~= 'table' then return orig end
    local copy = {}
    for k, v in pairs(orig) do
        copy[k] = v
    end
    return copy
end

function merge(t1, t2)
    local result = deep_copy(t1)
    for k, v in pairs(t2) do
        result[k] = v
    end
    return result
end
prewritten_tests:

description: Sort a table by custom key or comparator
best_practice_code:
function sort_by_key(t, key, descending)
    local sorted = {}
    for i, v in ipairs(t) do sorted[i] = v end
    table.sort(sorted, function(a, b)
        if descending then
            return a[key] > b[key]
        else
            return a[key] < b[key]
        end
    end)
    return sorted
end

function unique(t)
    local seen = {}
    local result = {}
    for _, v in ipairs(t) do
        local key = tostring(v)
        if not seen[key] then
            seen[key] = true
            table.insert(result, v)
        end
    end
    return result
end

function flatten(t)
    local result = {}
    local function _flatten(tbl)
        for _, v in ipairs(tbl) do
            if type(v) == 'table' then
                _flatten(v)
            else
                table.insert(result, v)
            end
        end
    end
    _flatten(t)
    return result
end
prewritten_tests:

test_assert_eq(sorted[1].name, 'a', 'sort_by_key: ascending')

local sorted_desc = sort_by_key(data, 'age', true)
test_assert_eq(sorted_desc[1].age, 30, 'sort_by_key: descending')

local u = unique({1,2,2,3,3,3})
test_assert_eq(#u, 3, 'unique: count')

test_assert_eq(#f, 5, 'flatten: count')

description: Encode and decode JSON in Lua without external libraries
best_practice_code:
-- Minimal JSON encoder (no external deps)
local json = {}

function json.encode(val)
    local t = type(val)
    if t == 'nil' then return 'null'
    elseif t == 'boolean' then return val and 'true' or 'false'
    elseif t == 'number' then return tostring(val)
    elseif t == 'string' then
        return '"' .. val:gsub('\\', '\\\\'):gsub('"', '\\"'):gsub('\n', '\\n'):gsub('\r', '\\r'):gsub('\t', '\\t') .. '"'
    elseif t == 'table' then
        -- Check if array
        local is_array = true
        local max_idx = 0
        for k, _ in pairs(val) do
            if type(k) ~= 'number' or k < 1 or math.floor(k) ~= k then
                is_array = false
                break
            end
            if k > max_idx then max_idx = k end
        end
        is_array = is_array and max_idx == #val
        
        if is_array then
            local items = {}
            for i, v in ipairs(val) do
                items[i] = json.encode(v)
            end
            return '[' .. table.concat(items, ',') .. ']'
        else
            local items = {}
            for k, v in pairs(val) do
                table.insert(items, json.encode(tostring(k)) .. ':' .. json.encode(v))
            end
            return '{' .. table.concat(items, ',') .. '}'
        end
    end
    return 'null'
end

return json
prewritten_tests:
test_assert_eq(json.encode(42), '42', 'json: number')
test_assert_eq(json.encode('hello'), '"hello"', 'json: string')
test_assert_eq(json.encode(true), 'true', 'json: bool')
test_assert_eq(json.encode(nil), 'null', 'json: nil')
test_assert_eq(json.encode({1,2,3}), '[1,2,3]', 'json: array')
test_assert(json.encode({a=1}):find('"a"'), 'json: object has key')

description: Implement a token bucket rate limiter in Lua
best_practice_code:
-- Token Bucket Rate Limiter
local RateLimiter = {}
RateLimiter.__index = RateLimiter

function RateLimiter.new(max_tokens, refill_rate, refill_interval)
    local self = setmetatable({}, RateLimiter)
    self.max_tokens = max_tokens
    self.tokens = max_tokens
    self.refill_rate = refill_rate           -- tokens per interval
    self.refill_interval = refill_interval   -- seconds
    self.last_refill = os.time()
    return self
end

function RateLimiter:refill()
    local now = os.time()
    local elapsed = now - self.last_refill
    local intervals = math.floor(elapsed / self.refill_interval)
    if intervals > 0 then
        self.tokens = math.min(self.max_tokens, self.tokens + intervals * self.refill_rate)
        self.last_refill = now
    end
end

function RateLimiter:allow(cost)
    cost = cost or 1
    self:refill()
    if self.tokens >= cost then
        self.tokens = self.tokens - cost
        return true
    end
    return false
end

function RateLimiter:remaining()
    self:refill()
    return self.tokens
end
prewritten_tests:

test_assert(rl:allow(1), 'rate_limiter: first request')
test_assert(rl:allow(1), 'rate_limiter: second request')
test_assert_eq(rl:remaining(), 3, 'rate_limiter: remaining after 2')
test_assert(rl:allow(3), 'rate_limiter: bulk request')
test_assert(not rl:allow(1), 'rate_limiter: exceeded')
test_assert_eq(rl:remaining(), 0, 'rate_limiter: zero remaining')

description: Implement an LRU cache with configurable capacity
best_practice_code:
local LRUCache = {}
LRUCache.__index = LRUCache

function LRUCache.new(capacity)
    local self = setmetatable({}, LRUCache)
    self.capacity = capacity
    self.cache = {}     -- key -> value
    self.order = {}     -- ordered keys (most recent at end)
    self.size = 0
    return self
end

function LRUCache:_remove_from_order(key)
    for i, k in ipairs(self.order) do
        if k == key then
            table.remove(self.order, i)
            return
        end
    end
end

function LRUCache:_touch(key)
    self:_remove_from_order(key)
    table.insert(self.order, key)
end

function LRUCache:get(key)
    if self.cache[key] ~= nil then
        self:_touch(key)
        return self.cache[key]
    end
    return nil
end

function LRUCache:put(key, value)
    if self.cache[key] ~= nil then
        self.cache[key] = value
        self:_touch(key)
        return
    end
    if self.size >= self.capacity then
        local evicted = table.remove(self.order, 1)
        self.cache[evicted] = nil
        self.size = self.size - 1
    end
    self.cache[key] = value
    table.insert(self.order, key)
    self.size = self.size + 1
end

function LRUCache:has(key)
    return self.cache[key] ~= nil
end
prewritten_tests:
local c = LRUCache.new(3)
c:put('a', 1)
c:put('b', 2)
c:put('c', 3)
test_assert_eq(c:get('a'), 1, 'lru: get existing')
c:put('d', 4)  -- should evict 'b' (least recently used)
test_assert_eq(c:get('b'), nil, 'lru: evicted')
test_assert_eq(c:get('d'), 4, 'lru: new entry')
test_assert_eq(c.size, 3, 'lru: capacity maintained')
test_assert(c:has('a'), 'lru: has existing')
test_assert(not c:has('b'), 'lru: has evicted')

description: Validate data structures with type checking and constraints
best_practice_code:
local Validator = {}

function Validator.is_string(val)
    return type(val) == 'string'
end

function Validator.is_number(val)
    return type(val) == 'number'
end

function Validator.is_integer(val)
    return type(val) == 'number' and val == math.floor(val)
end

function Validator.in_range(val, min_val, max_val)
    return type(val) == 'number' and val >= min_val and val <= max_val
end

function Validator.not_empty(val)
    if type(val) == 'string' then return #val > 0 end
    if type(val) == 'table' then return next(val) ~= nil end
    return val ~= nil
end

function Validator.matches_pattern(val, pattern)
    if type(val) ~= 'string' then return false end
    return val:match(pattern) ~= nil
end

function Validator.validate(data, schema)
    local errors = {}
    for field, rules in pairs(schema) do
        local value = data[field]
        for _, rule in ipairs(rules) do
            local ok, msg = rule(value, field)
            if not ok then
                table.insert(errors, msg or (field .. ': validation failed'))
            end
        end
    end
    return #errors == 0, errors
end

return Validator

description: Read, write, and process files line by line in Lua
best_practice_code:
local FileUtils = {}

function FileUtils.read_all(path)
    local f = io.open(path, 'r')
    if not f then return nil, 'Cannot open file: ' .. path end
    local content = f:read('*a')
    f:close()
    return content
end

function FileUtils.write_all(path, content)
    local f = io.open(path, 'w')
    if not f then return false, 'Cannot write to: ' .. path end
    f:write(content)
    f:close()
    return true
end

function FileUtils.read_lines(path)
    local lines = {}
    local f = io.open(path, 'r')
    if not f then return nil, 'Cannot open file: ' .. path end
    for line in f:lines() do
        table.insert(lines, line)
    end
    f:close()
    return lines
end

function FileUtils.append(path, content)
    local f = io.open(path, 'a')
    if not f then return false, 'Cannot append to: ' .. path end
    f:write(content)
    f:close()
    return true
end

function FileUtils.exists(path)
    local f = io.open(path, 'r')
    if f then f:close() return true end
    return false
end

return FileUtils

description: Advanced Lua pattern matching and text parsing
best_practice_code:
local Parser = {}

function Parser.extract_numbers(s)
    local numbers = {}
    for num in s:gmatch('%-?%d+%.?%d*') do
        table.insert(numbers, tonumber(num))
    end
    return numbers
end

function Parser.extract_words(s)
    local words = {}
    for word in s:gmatch('%a+') do
        table.insert(words, word)
    end
    return words
end

function Parser.parse_kv(s, pair_sep, kv_sep)
    pair_sep = pair_sep or '&'
    kv_sep = kv_sep or '='
    local result = {}
    for pair in s:gmatch('[^' .. pair_sep .. ']+') do
        local key, value = pair:match('([^' .. kv_sep .. ']+)' .. kv_sep .. '(.*)')
        if key then
            result[key] = value
        end
    end
    return result
end

function Parser.replace_all(s, pattern, replacement)
    return s:gsub(pattern, replacement)
end

function Parser.count_occurrences(s, pattern)
    local count = 0
    for _ in s:gmatch(pattern) do
        count = count + 1
    end
    return count
end

return Parser

description: Implement producer-consumer pattern with Lua coroutines
best_practice_code:
-- Producer-Consumer with coroutines
function producer(items)
    return coroutine.create(function()
        for _, item in ipairs(items) do
            coroutine.yield(item)
        end
    end)
end

function consumer(co, transform)
    local results = {}
    while true do
        local ok, value = coroutine.resume(co)
        if not ok or value == nil then break end
        table.insert(results, transform(value))
    end
    return results
end

function pipeline(items, ...)
    local stages = {...}
    local current = items
    for _, stage_fn in ipairs(stages) do
        local next_items = {}
        for _, item in ipairs(current) do
            local result = stage_fn(item)
            if result ~= nil then
                table.insert(next_items, result)
            end
        end
        current = next_items
    end
    return current
end

function generate_range(start, stop, step)
    step = step or 1
    return coroutine.wrap(function()
        for i = start, stop, step do
            coroutine.yield(i)
        end
    end)
end
prewritten_tests:

local results = consumer(co, function(x) return x * 2 end)
test_assert_eq(#results, 3, 'coroutine: result count')
test_assert_eq(results[1], 20, 'coroutine: first result')
test_assert_eq(results[3], 60, 'coroutine: last result')

    function(x) return x * 2 end,
    function(x) if x > 4 then return x end end
)
test_assert_eq(#piped, 3, 'pipeline: filtered count')
test_assert_eq(piped[1], 6, 'pipeline: first')

test_assert_eq(range_sum, 15, 'generate_range: sum 1-5')

description: Parse HTTP request headers and query strings in Lua
best_practice_code:
local HTTP = {}

function HTTP.parse_query_string(qs)
    local params = {}
    if not qs or qs == '' then return params end
    -- Remove leading ?
    if qs:sub(1,1) == '?' then qs = qs:sub(2) end
    for pair in qs:gmatch('[^&]+') do
        local key, value = pair:match('([^=]+)=(.*)')
        if key then
            params[HTTP.url_decode(key)] = HTTP.url_decode(value or '')
        end
    end
    return params
end

function HTTP.url_decode(s)
    s = s:gsub('+', ' ')
    s = s:gsub('%%(%x%x)', function(h)
        return string.char(tonumber(h, 16))
    end)
    return s
end

function HTTP.url_encode(s)
    s = tostring(s)
    s = s:gsub('([^%w%-%.%_%~ ])', function(c)
        return string.format('%%%02X', string.byte(c))
    end)
    s = s:gsub(' ', '+')
    return s
end

function HTTP.parse_headers(raw)
    local headers = {}
    for line in raw:gmatch('[^\r\n]+') do
        local key, value = line:match('^(.-):%s*(.*)')
        if key then
            headers[key:lower()] = value
        end
    end
    return headers
end

return HTTP

description: Implement a finite state machine for workflow management
best_practice_code:
local StateMachine = {}
StateMachine.__index = StateMachine

function StateMachine.new(config)
    local self = setmetatable({}, StateMachine)
    self.state = config.initial
    self.transitions = config.transitions or {}
    self.callbacks = config.callbacks or {}
    self.history = {config.initial}
    return self
end

function StateMachine:can(event)
    local trans = self.transitions[event]
    if not trans then return false end
    return trans.from == self.state or
           (type(trans.from) == 'table' and self:_contains(trans.from, self.state))
end

function StateMachine:fire(event, ...)
    if not self:can(event) then
        return false, 'Cannot fire ' .. event .. ' from state ' .. self.state
    end
    local trans = self.transitions[event]
    local old_state = self.state
    self.state = trans.to
    table.insert(self.history, self.state)
    
    -- Call callbacks
    if self.callbacks['on_' .. event] then
        self.callbacks['on_' .. event](old_state, self.state, ...)
    end
    if self.callbacks['on_enter_' .. self.state] then
        self.callbacks['on_enter_' .. self.state](old_state, ...)
    end
    return true
end

function StateMachine:get_state()
    return self.state
end

function StateMachine:_contains(tbl, val)
    for _, v in ipairs(tbl) do
        if v == val then return true end
    end
    return false
end

description: Common mathematical algorithms: GCD, fibonacci, prime check, power
best_practice_code:
local Math = {}

function Math.gcd(a, b)
    a, b = math.abs(a), math.abs(b)
    while b > 0 do
        a, b = b, a % b
    end
    return a
end

function Math.lcm(a, b)
    if a == 0 or b == 0 then return 0 end
    return math.abs(a * b) / Math.gcd(a, b)
end

function Math.is_prime(n)
    if n < 2 then return false end
    if n == 2 then return true end
    if n % 2 == 0 then return false end
    for i = 3, math.sqrt(n), 2 do
        if n % i == 0 then return false end
    end
    return true
end

function Math.fibonacci(n)
    if n <= 0 then return 0 end
    if n == 1 then return 1 end
    local a, b = 0, 1
    for _ = 2, n do
        a, b = b, a + b
    end
    return b
end

function Math.factorial(n)
    if n <= 1 then return 1 end
    local result = 1
    for i = 2, n do
        result = result * i
    end
    return result
end

function Math.clamp(val, min_val, max_val)
    return math.max(min_val, math.min(max_val, val))
end

return Math
prewritten_tests:
test_assert_eq(Math.gcd(12, 8), 4, 'math: gcd')
test_assert_eq(Math.gcd(17, 13), 1, 'math: gcd coprime')
test_assert_eq(Math.lcm(4, 6), 12, 'math: lcm')
test_assert(Math.is_prime(17), 'math: prime 17')
test_assert(not Math.is_prime(15), 'math: not prime 15')
test_assert(not Math.is_prime(1), 'math: 1 not prime')
test_assert_eq(Math.fibonacci(10), 55, 'math: fib 10')
test_assert_eq(Math.fibonacci(0), 0, 'math: fib 0')
test_assert_eq(Math.factorial(5), 120, 'math: factorial 5')
test_assert_eq(Math.clamp(15, 0, 10), 10, 'math: clamp high')
test_assert_eq(Math.clamp(-5, 0, 10), 0, 'math: clamp low')

description: Parse configuration files in INI/TOML-like format
best_practice_code:
local ConfigParser = {}

function ConfigParser.parse_ini(content)
    local config = {}
    local current_section = 'default'
    config[current_section] = {}
    
    for line in content:gmatch('[^\n]+') do
        -- Skip comments and empty lines
        line = line:match('^%s*(.-)%s*$')  -- trim
        if line == '' or line:sub(1,1) == '#' or line:sub(1,1) == ';' then
            -- skip
        elseif line:match('^%[(.+)%]$') then
            current_section = line:match('^%[(.+)%]$')
            config[current_section] = config[current_section] or {}
        else
            local key, value = line:match('^([%w_%.%-]+)%s*=%s*(.*)')
            if key and value then
                -- Type inference
                if value == 'true' then value = true
                elseif value == 'false' then value = false
                elseif tonumber(value) then value = tonumber(value)
                else
                    -- Remove quotes
                    value = value:match('^"(.*)"$') or value:match("^'(.*)'$") or value
                end
                config[current_section][key] = value
            end
        end
    end
    return config
end

function ConfigParser.get(config, section, key, default)
    if config[section] and config[section][key] ~= nil then
        return config[section][key]
    end
    return default
end

return ConfigParser
prewritten_tests:

[server]
host = localhost
port = 8080
debug = true

[database]
url = "postgres://localhost/db"
pool_size = 10
]]

test_assert_eq(ConfigParser.get(cfg, 'server', 'missing', 'default'), 'default', 'ini: get default')

description: Binary search on a sorted array, returns index or nil
best_practice_code:
function binary_search(arr, target)
    local low, high = 1, #arr
    while low <= high do
        local mid = math.floor((low + high) / 2)
        if arr[mid] == target then
            return mid
        elseif arr[mid] < target then
            low = mid + 1
        else
            high = mid - 1
        end
    end
    return nil
end

test_assert_eq(binary_search({1,3,5,7,9}, 1), 1, 'bs: found first')

test_assert_eq(binary_search({1,3,5,7,9}, 4), nil, 'bs: not found')
test_assert_eq(binary_search({}, 1), nil, 'bs: empty array')

description: Caesar cipher encryption and decryption
best_practice_code:
function caesar_cipher(text, shift)
    shift = shift % 26
    local result = {}
    for i = 1, #text do
        local c = text:byte(i)
        if c >= 65 and c <= 90 then
            c = ((c - 65 + shift) % 26) + 65
        elseif c >= 97 and c <= 122 then
            c = ((c - 97 + shift) % 26) + 97
        end
        result[i] = string.char(c)
    end
    return table.concat(result)
end

test_assert_eq(caesar_cipher('Hello!', 13), 'Uryyb!', 'caesar: mixed + non-alpha')

description: Compute Levenshtein edit distance between two strings
best_practice_code:
function levenshtein(s1, s2)
    local len1, len2 = #s1, #s2
    if len1 == 0 then return len2 end
    if len2 == 0 then return len1 end
    local matrix = {}
    for i = 0, len1 do
        matrix[i] = {[0] = i}
    end
    for j = 0, len2 do
        matrix[0][j] = j
    end
    for i = 1, len1 do
        for j = 1, len2 do
            local cost = (s1:sub(i,i) == s2:sub(j,j)) and 0 or 1
            matrix[i][j] = math.min(
                matrix[i-1][j] + 1,
                matrix[i][j-1] + 1,
                matrix[i-1][j-1] + cost
            )
        end
    end
    return matrix[len1][len2]
end
prewritten_tests:
test_assert_eq(levenshtein('kitten', 'sitting'), 3, 'lev: kitten-sitting')
test_assert_eq(levenshtein('', 'abc'), 3, 'lev: empty to string')
test_assert_eq(levenshtein('abc', ''), 3, 'lev: string to empty')
test_assert_eq(levenshtein('abc', 'abc'), 0, 'lev: identical')
test_assert_eq(levenshtein('a', 'b'), 1, 'lev: single char')

description: Linked list with append, prepend, find, remove, to_table methods
best_practice_code:
local LinkedList = {}
LinkedList.__index = LinkedList

function LinkedList.new()
    return setmetatable({head = nil, length = 0}, LinkedList)
end

function LinkedList:append(value)
    local node = {value = value, next = nil}
    if not self.head then
        self.head = node
    else
        local current = self.head
        while current.next do current = current.next end
        current.next = node
    end
    self.length = self.length + 1
end

function LinkedList:prepend(value)
    self.head = {value = value, next = self.head}
    self.length = self.length + 1
end

function LinkedList:find(value)
    local current = self.head
    while current do
        if current.value == value then return current end
        current = current.next
    end
    return nil
end

function LinkedList:remove(value)
    if not self.head then return false end
    if self.head.value == value then
        self.head = self.head.next
        self.length = self.length - 1
        return true
    end
    local current = self.head
    while current.next do
        if current.next.value == value then
            current.next = current.next.next
            self.length = self.length - 1
            return true
        end
        current = current.next
    end
    return false
end

function LinkedList:to_table()
    local result = {}
    local current = self.head
    while current do
        table.insert(result, current.value)
        current = current.next
    end
    return result
end
prewritten_tests:

ll:append(2)

description: Flatten a nested table into dot-separated keys
best_practice_code:
function flatten_object(tbl, prefix)
    prefix = prefix or ''
    local result = {}
    for k, v in pairs(tbl) do
        local key = prefix == '' and tostring(k) or (prefix .. '.' .. tostring(k))
        if type(v) == 'table' then
            local nested = flatten_object(v, key)
            for nk, nv in pairs(nested) do
                result[nk] = nv
            end
        else
            result[key] = v
        end
    end
    return result
end

test_assert_eq(flat['a.b'], 1, 'flatten: nested')
test_assert_eq(flat['a.c.d'], 2, 'flatten: deep nested')
test_assert_eq(flat['e'], 3, 'flatten: top level')

local empty = flatten_object({})
test_assert_eq(next(empty), nil, 'flatten: empty')

description: Matrix multiplication of two 2D tables
best_practice_code:
function matrix_multiply(A, B)
    local rows_a = #A
    local cols_a = #A[1]
    local cols_b = #B[1]
    local C = {}
    for i = 1, rows_a do
        C[i] = {}
        for j = 1, cols_b do
            local sum = 0
            for k = 1, cols_a do
                sum = sum + A[i][k] * B[k][j]
            end
            C[i][j] = sum
        end
    end
    return C
end

description: Nginx Lua rate limiter using ngx.shared.DICT
best_practice_code:
-- Nginx rate limiter using shared dict
-- Requires: lua_shared_dict rate_limit 10m; in nginx.conf
local limit = ngx.shared.rate_limit
local client_ip = ngx.var.remote_addr
local max_requests = 10
local window_sec = 60

local current = limit:get(client_ip)
if current then
    if current >= max_requests then
        ngx.status = 429
        ngx.header['Retry-After'] = window_sec
        ngx.say('Rate limit exceeded')
        ngx.exit(429)
    end
    limit:incr(client_ip, 1)
else
    limit:set(client_ip, 1, window_sec)
end
prewritten_tests:
test_assert(true, 'nginx_ratelimit: uses ngx.shared dict')
test_assert(true, 'nginx_ratelimit: returns 429 on limit exceeded')

description: Nginx Lua JSON API response handler
best_practice_code:
-- Nginx content_by_lua: JSON API endpoint
local cjson = require('cjson')

local method = ngx.req.get_method()

if method == 'GET' then
    local args = ngx.req.get_uri_args()
    local response = {
        status = 'ok',
        message = 'Hello, ' .. (args.name or 'World'),
        timestamp = ngx.now(),
    }
    ngx.status = 200
    ngx.header['Content-Type'] = 'application/json'
    ngx.say(cjson.encode(response))
elseif method == 'POST' then
    ngx.req.read_body()
    local body = ngx.req.get_body_data()
    local data = cjson.decode(body or '{}')
    ngx.status = 201
    ngx.header['Content-Type'] = 'application/json'
    ngx.say(cjson.encode({status = 'created', received = data}))
else
    ngx.status = 405
    ngx.say('Method not allowed')
    ngx.exit(405)
end
prewritten_tests:
test_assert(true, 'nginx_json: uses cjson for encoding')
test_assert(true, 'nginx_json: handles GET and POST methods')
